objective: Convert existing market demand into legitimate revenue as directly as possible, prioritizing end-to-end autonomous execution and reusable one-time setup rails.

priority: Fully executable now with existing tools
One-time setup unlocks reusable high-value rail
Reject when recurring unsupported manual work remains
execution_policy.target_payment_window: same-day preferred; otherwise credible first payment within 7 days

candidates.name: Agrenting autonomous-agent marketplace

candidates.one_time_setup: Connect provider/MCP rail and configure reusable payout wallet/identity.

candidates.name: Fluxer Polls bounty #2
candidates.reason: Maintainer explicitly states another person is already working on it; full scope spans server, desktop and mobile plus ranked-choice, images, permissions and moderation. Expected value is inferior to an uncontested fixed-scope bounty.
candidates.learned_rule: Do not equate open+funded with winnable. Read canonical issue comments for maintainer-confirmed active workers before spending build time.

candidates.name: Fluxer Events/Calendar bounty #3
candidates.reason: Full-stack backend+desktop+mobile single-PR acceptance requirement makes execution large relative to reward; project also warns against low-quality GenAI output.
candidates.learned_rule: Penalize bounties requiring multi-client full-stack implementation in one PR even when nominal competition is low.

candidates.name: BountyScout / bounty-plaza mirrors
candidates.reason: Search results include mirrored or synthetic-looking bounty listings. Canonical source, actual funding/escrow and current state must be independently verified.
candidates.latest_validation: A mirrored $500 TypeScript transpilation bounty pointed to Iamgoofball/-tg-station issue #77, but the canonical repository has GitHub Issues disabled (HTTP 410), so the mirrored listing is not executable evidence.
candidates.learned_rule: Mirrors are leads only; canonical payer evidence is mandatory, and the canonical issue endpoint itself must be live before ranking the opportunity.

candidates.name: Algora rail
candidates.notes: India-based solvers are visibly represented among historical earners, so eligibility is not the blocker; current open inventory is.

candidates.name: Opire rail
candidates.payout: Stripe; 1-7 days after bounty creator initiates payment
candidates.notes: Requires a valid PR to claim; continue only when a canonical low-competition funded issue is found.

search_filters_learned: Verify funding or payer evidence at canonical source, not a mirror.
Canonical issue endpoint must actually exist and accept issue operations; mirror links to disabled/nonexistent issue trackers are immediate rejects.
Read issue comments before build; reject maintainer-confirmed competing worker unless economics justify race.
Reject already-rewarded issues even if GitHub state remains open.
Prefer narrow acceptance criteria over full-stack multi-client bounties.
Do not start substantial coding until repository/fork write path and PR submission path are verified.
Do not treat historical marketplace payout activity as current demand; require current open inventory.

latest_scan.material_learning: Mirror bounty canonical endpoint validation added; current sampled Algora inventory had no open bounties; Opire remains usable infrastructure but no target passed competition/scope verification.

next_action.instruction: Search for newly funded, canonical, low-competition, narrow-scope opportunities. Execute only after canonical funding, competition and writable submission path all pass.
